title: Nyaya (logic)
hook: a shape at dusk could be a post or a person, and Nyaya says that moment of not knowing is where its whole path begins

segments.voice: Yesterday, the hetvabhasa: a reason that only looks like one. Today is the last day with Nyaya.
screen: `HOLD YOUR OWN UP TO THE LIGHT.` · `NYAYA, A LAST DAY.`

segments.voice: It's getting dark on a country road. Up ahead, at the edge of a field, a tall, thin shape stands perfectly still. A wooden post? A person, waiting? You can see height, and that it's upright. But the detail that would settle it, a hand, a face, the grain of the wood, isn't there yet. For a few seconds, you simply don't know. Nyaya teachers use this very picture, the post or the person at dusk, for doubt. And they don't treat it as a failure of the mind. They treat it as a doorway.
screen: `A SHAPE AT DUSK.` → `A POST, OR A PERSON?` → `NOT KNOWING, AS A DOORWAY.`

segments.voice: The Nyaya Sutra names doubt, samshaya, among the things a seeker must understand. Doubt is a mind pulled between two possibilities, because it sees what they share and can't yet see what tells them apart. Vatsyayana, its early commentator, makes a quiet point: nobody inquires into what is completely unknown, or into what is already settled. Inquiry lives in between, in doubt. In the Sutra's opening list, doubt comes right after the means of knowing and the things to be known, ahead of the example, the parts of an argument and the conclusion. Doubt isn't a detour on the way to reasoning. It's what gets reasoning going. The post and the person share height and stillness; that's why you're stuck. So the way out isn't to stare harder at what they share. It's to look for the one mark only one of them has: a hand that moves, a bird landing on top, the grain of the wood. What would tell these apart? On the first Nyaya day you met the chain that runs from false knowledge to pain, and the release that comes when false knowledge goes. Handled well, doubt stops one piece of false knowledge at the door. Rush it, and you call the post a person and run, or call the person a post and walk past someone who needed help. Stay with it honestly, and one small thing gets seen as it is. For Nyaya, that small seeing belongs to the same work that ends in apavarga, release. Tomorrow, a close neighbor asks not how we know, but what there is to know.
screen: `SAMSHAYA: DOUBT STARTS THE SEARCH.` · `DOUBT COMES RIGHT AFTER KNOWING.` · `LOOK FOR WHAT TELLS THEM APART.` · `APAVARGA: RELEASE.` · then, large: `WHAT WOULD TELL THESE APART?`

segments.voice: Bring to mind one thing you honestly don't know yet, and don't rush to call it post or person. Notice what the two possibilities share and what would tell them apart; when the mind grabs at an answer, come back to the breath. If you pray, you can hold the question before God and simply wait.
Nyaya. Today, samshaya, doubt: the mind caught between two, where honest inquiry begins, on a path that aims at release.
Your line: Nyaya, logic. Honest doubt is a doorway, not a failure. Day one thousand one hundred sixty-five, done.

howItsDone: In the Nyaya tradition, study of logic is understood as part of the path to liberation; students begin with the opening sutras of the Nyaya Sutra, which tie true knowledge to the highest good.
